description: fetchngs writes a sarek samplesheet (patient = the ENA sample accession) with --nf-core-pipeline sarek; it has no lane, so each run's accession becomes its lane — sarek needs patient, sample and lane to be unique together; sarek reads paired-end FastQ only, so every row needs a fastq_2. No status or sex column is written: sarek treats every sample as normal tissue (status 0, sex NA) and runs germline analyses only; a tumour/normal design needs its own sarek samplesheet (a handoff's set gives every row the same value). Runs whose ENA instrument_platform is not a short-read platform (the ones nf-core/mag accepts as short reads: ILLUMINA, BGISEQ, DNBSEQ, ELEMENT, ULTIMA, ION_TORRENT, LS454, …) are refused: sarek analyses short reads, and long-read, capillary or colour-space runs would be processed as if they were.
